title: 100 years of the red trucks: Nuevo Laredo's firefighters celebrate a century of service
excerpt: Nuevo Laredo's fire corps turns 100 this October. The milestone is being marked with specialized Incident Command System training for some 90 emergency personnel from government agencies, utilities and private industry, as the city's fleet grows to 35 operational units.
content:
A century ago, Nuevo Laredo's first firefighters rolled out with little more than courage and whatever equipment the city could spare. This October, the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Nuevo Laredo completes 100 years of service — and the municipal government is marking the milestone by making today's emergency crews better prepared than any that came before them, according to Agencia de Noticias Oficina de Corresponsales and CML Noticias (Oct. 20, 2026).

The centerpiece is a specialized training course in the Incident Command System (Sistema de Comando de Incidentes), designed to tighten coordination among Protección Civil, firefighters, government institutions and private companies so that emergency response is faster and more effective across the city.

The city's director of Protección Civil and Bomberos, Humberto Fernández, told reporters that 65 participants initially registered for the course, with 25 more elements joining afterward — bringing the total to roughly 90. Fernández described the course as a valuable opportunity for firefighters to learn, stay current and earn certification.

The roster of participants reflects just how many moving parts a border-city emergency can involve. Taking part alongside municipal crews are representatives of the Comisión Federal de Electricidad (CFE), Naturgy, LP gas companies, the Red Cross, Pemex, the maquiladora mutual-aid committee CLAM, the Comité de Ayuda Mutua (CAM), firefighters from Nuevo León and Tamaulipas, and personnel from the Quetzalcóatl International Airport, in addition to staff from primary public services and public works.

The program blends theory with hands-on practice: trainees reviewed valves, connections and components of tank cars and road tankers that move chemicals by rail and highway, and worked with the chemical emergency response guide. The focus is no accident — in a city whose economy runs on the movement of goods and hazardous substances, knowing how to read risk is part of the job.

Fernández also pointed to a growing fleet behind the city's emergency response. Nuevo Laredo counts 35 operational units, and during 2026 the corps added two new fire trucks, three rapid-attack units, ambulances and water tankers — equipment that he said improves response times and working conditions for personnel.

The city's firefighting capacity also reaches beyond its borders. Fernández said local crews have provided support in municipalities across Tamaulipas, Nuevo León and Coahuila, as well as along the highways that converge on Nuevo Laredo. "We have a region we are covering," he said, pointing to the new equipment as what lets the city answer any contingency.

Sources: Agencia de Noticias Oficina de Corresponsales, "Fortalece Gobierno Municipal atención y protocolos de Protección Civil y Bomberos ante emergencias con certificación en sistema de comando de incidentes" (Oct. 20, 2026); CML Noticias, "Capacitan a cuerpos de emergencia en Nuevo Laredo para mejorar respuesta ante incidentes" (Oct. 20, 2026).
